articles.title: ‘The food of emperors’: a Chinese restaurant turns boring turkeys into crispy showstoppers
articles.summary: Chicago’s Sun Wah BBQ started a new Turkey Day tradition for immigrants and other neighbors: allowing them to bring in their fowl and roast it in the fragrant Hong Kong-style. Tell us: do you have a special new year food tradition?
body: Behind an Uptown Chicago facade of glass and green-glazed bricks, rows of mahogany-red ducks glisten.

This neighborhood is sometimes called “New Chinatown”, sometimes “Little Vietnam ”. And this tidy restaurant is Sun Wah BBQ, which Eric and Lynda Cheng opened in 1987. Today, it’s also an unlikely Thanksgiving destination.

Every November, customers bring their own turkeys to Sun Wah to be prepared in the style of a Hong Kong roast duck. This year, the Cheng family will roast close to 200 turkeys, thanks to a TikTok video that increased demand. But this annual tradition, turning pale workaday turkeys into gorgeously lacquered holiday centerpieces, began as an informal favor about two decades ago.

body: Let’s be honest, side dishes are the true workhorses of Thanksgiving dinner. From a classic green been casserole perfected by Hetty Lui McKinnon to Yotam Ottolenghi’s twist on stuffing, here are nine of our go-to trimmings for Thanksgiving dinner. Or explore more from our huge collection.
Rukmini Iyer’s jewelled winter salad adds a burst of color to any spread. Iyer recommends roasting the squash the day before and marinating the beans overnight.

Heat the oven to 390F. Mix the squash, two tablespoons of olive oil, the ras el hanout and salt in a roasting tray large enough to hold everything in a single layer. In a small bowl, toss the onion wedges with half the lemon juice (this will help them keep their colour), add them to the squash tray, then roast for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, put the remaining oil, the garlic and lemon zest in a large frying pan over a low heat, and warm through for two to three minutes without letting the garlic brown. Add the butter beans, cook, stirring occasionally, for six to seven minutes, then take off the heat.

articles.title: 8 Best Gua Sha Tools to Expertly Sculpt, Lift, and Tone
articles.summary: From Lanshin, Osea, and more, the best gua sha tools can contour the skin, boost circulation, and promote lymphatic drainage to reveal a glowing complexion.
body: Over the last few years, lymphatic drainage has gone from an IYKYK technique to an all-out wellness obsession. Oft described as the “Cinderella of medicine,” the lymphatic system is responsible for collecting excess fluid from tissues, transporting immune cells, and carrying certain waste products away from cells. This system, however, doesn’t work on its own to get the lymph flowing. Lymphatic drainage is a more manual practice; you can try your hand at deep breathing or dry brushing, but few things offer offer as excellent lifting benefits as the best gua sha tools.

“The literal gua sha Mandarin translation is ‘to scrape sand,’” explains Lin Chen, cofounder of Pink Moon. “Gua sha tools have been used as a unique approach for holistic healing in China for 4,000 years. It has been traditionally used over the body to help aid in the movement of qi (which is energy flow), increase circulation, and release tension.” That said, Chen continues saying that research shows that the practice was first used in the Paleolithic Ages, dating back to the Ming dynasty in China.

articles.title: The New Rules of Complexion Makeup
articles.summary: The Vogue Beauty Board weighs in on the new era of complexion makeup. From skin tints to full-coverage foundations, expect better shade ranges, lightweight textures, and your-skin-but-better finishes.
body: A decade ago, many of us wouldn’t leave the house without a full-coverage beat. As Instagram selfies and YouTube tutorials took over pop culture, meticulously sculpted, perfected complexions reigned supreme—until the pendulum swung in the opposite direction, ushering in an era of barely-there coverage and skin-care-infused formulas. And while the early 2020s were defined by ultra-dewy, almost damp-looking skin, today’s complexion ideal strikes a more nuanced balance: coverage without the weight, radiance without the shine.

“Modern complexion formulations have come such a long way, and the new-Gen complexion products give medium to buildable coverage that glides and melts into skin, while giving a soft-focus matte finish that reads radiant rather than shiny,” says celebrity makeup artist and Vogue Beauty Board member Fara Homidi. “We can now get more coverage, while the final look is breathable and has flex to it, never heavy and cakey.” Nowadays, lightweight texture, skin-friendly ingredients, and flexible coverage are non-negotiable. The ideal product perfects your complexion without looking or feeling like makeup.
points: The Vogue Beauty Board weighs in on the new era of complexion makeup.

articles.title: For Malin Åkerman, ‘The Hunting Wives’ Is (Still) a Dream Come True
articles.summary: Ahead of the release of “The Hunting Wives” season two, Åkerman talks to Vogue about the Margo Bankses in her own life, performing with Brittany Snow at the Las Culturistas Culture Awards, and why it’s the perfect time to watch a show about lesbians in Texas.
body: “Girl, that one’s always a good one,” Malin Åkerman says. I’ve just told her how many times I’ve rewatched her 2008 rom-com 27 Dresses, in which she played the charming, wedding dress-and-crush-stealing Tess, younger sister to Katherine Heigl’s responsible Jane. Tess is, in my view, one of the great 2000s-era villains—though Åkerman doesn’t see her as such.

“She was just a young, stupid girl who fell in love, and it was really wrong. That’s your sister’s crush. Don’t do that, girl. Not cool.” She laughs. “But there was a life lesson in it, and she learned and she grew from it. It’s less villain, more just human.”

Some of that sympathy also exists in the way Åkerman plays the audacious, gun-toting, bisexual Texas queen Margo Banks in Netflix’s The Hunting Wives, based on May Cobb’s novel, which returns for season two this week. Margo has done some bad things, but she’s certainly looked good doing ’em—and former Democratic campaign strategist Sophie (Brittany Snow) can’t help but be drawn into her orbit. Their Bonnie-and-Clyde love story continues in the new season, and the stakes have never been higher.
Vogue: It’s a great time to be releasing a show about Texas.

articles.title: “Do You Like It? Would You Wear It? Would You Buy It?”—An Oral History of Marc by Marc Jacobs
articles.summary: On the 25th anniversary of the now-shuttered label, we look at the influence and lasting legacy of Marc by Marc Jacobs, told by the people who shaped it.
body: And, oh, the stores. Jacobs’s shops helped transform a once sleepy stretch of the West Village into a destination, with six outposts within walking distance of each other. Among them was the Marc by Marc Jacobs accessories store, the pièce de résistance for tourists and broke fashion kids alike. Whether it was your first trip to New York or your tenth, you lined up on Bleecker. Tote bags came stamped with the most iconic run-on sentence in fashion history: Jacobs by Marc Jacobs for Marc by Marc Jacobs in Collaboration with Marc Jacobs for Marc by Marc Jacobs. With a simple tongue-twister, Jacobs let us all in on the joke.

Marc by Marc Jacobs was folded into Marc Jacobs in 2015, but it lives on as a moment of accessible cool that can’t be replicated. For those who worked on it, its magic was in the freedom they were given to create. Twenty-five years after it was first launched, we spoke with members of its creative team about the vintage hunts, the last-minute fittings, and how they were able to recreate the downtown cool around them for the runway.
